Declare `.external_worktrees/default-workspace-template` as a second reviewed repo in `.reviewer/settings.json`, so the code-guardian stop hook gates work done there (its own commits, gates, and PR) instead of only the monorepo's.

The nested worktree is only present in checkouts actively working on the default workspace template; in every other checkout the entry is skipped, leaving the hook's behavior unchanged. This requires code-guardian 0.3.0 or newer -- earlier versions treated an absent entry as a misconfiguration and blocked the hook.

`just dwt-worktree` now writes `.reviewer/settings.local.json` into the checkout it creates, turning the gates on for it: autofix and architecture verification, base branch `main`, and base-branch merge plus push on each stop, with a PR required before its CI is polled. The clean-tree check stays on there too, with one path exempted via code-guardian's `stop_hook.uncommitted_exempt_paths` (also new in 0.3.0): `system/vendor/mngr`, which `just minds-start` rsyncs the live mngr tree into, deliberately leaving it uncommitted -- review of that subtree's content is owned by the mngr repo's own PRs. The template repo's own committed config stays as it is, since that one governs agents running inside a workspace container, where the gates are deliberately off.
